Photoreal live-action, London, March 1881, gas jet from the left, black shadow, 35 mm film grain.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:07. The shot begins from <Picture 2>: a wide of the small charge room at night: the white-faced Inspector behind the high wooden desk with a steel pen over the open ledger, Jefferson Hope in the long brownish driving coat standing before the desk with his wrists manacled in front of him, the gas jet burning above the desk at the left, the bench along the right wall black. The camera is at the panelled door at a standing man's eye, four long strides from the desk, a 35mm lens. The gas jet comes from the LEFT above the desk. At the first frame the high wooden desk stands at the LEFT third of the frame the height of the middle third with the Inspector behind it and the gas jet at the TOP LEFT. Jefferson Hope stands before the desk at the CENTRE of the frame. The camera pushes in on the desk across the whole shot, travelling a hand's breadth as the gas flame flutters in its bracket, from 00:00 to 00:02. At 00:02 a steel pen dips to the ledger. At 00:05 the manacles' chain swings a finger's breadth, and the swing continues to the last frame of the shot. By 00:07 the camera is pushing in through the last frame, and the action continues with it.
